transcript.text: Just had a new induction hob fitted, Beko. When I put my saucepan on it just flashes a U and doesn't heat. Is it faulty? It's brand new!!

It is likely not faulty, as a flashing 'U' on induction hobs often simply means it cannot detect a suitable pan rather than indicating a breakdown. Since I cannot confirm the exact meaning of this code for your specific Beko model without the manual, we should look at the most common simple causes first. Please try placing a large, flat-based saucepan that you know works on another induction hob onto the zone; if it heats up, the issue is just cookware compatibility or placement. Ensure the pan base is completely dry and clean, as moisture or dirt can sometimes prevent the sensor from detecting the metal correctly.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
I don't have another induction hob to try it on! But I did put my cast-iron casserole on one zone and that heated fine. It's only my saucepans that flash the U. Why would that be?

That suggests the hob itself is working correctly, so the 'U' flash on your saucepans is almost certainly because they are not suitable for induction cooking. Induction hobs only heat magnetic pans of a specific size and material, and many standard saucepans lack the necessary ferrous base to trigger the heating element. To check if this is the case, try sticking a magnet to the bottom of one of your saucepans; if it does not stick firmly, that pan will never work on an induction hob. If you have any other pans with flat, magnetic bases, those should heat up without showing the code.
I tried a fridge magnet and it doesn't stick to any of my saucepans, but it does stick to the cast-iron casserole. So are my saucepans just no good for this hob?!

Yes, your saucepans are simply no good for this hob because they are not magnetic. Induction hobs only work with cookware that has a ferrous metal base, which is why the magnet sticks to your cast-iron casserole but not your saucepans. Since we have confirmed the hob works and the issue is just incompatible pans, I need to find out if there is anything else going on or if you need help finding compatible replacements. Could you please provide the model number of your Beko hob? It is usually found on a label on the underside of the unit or on your guarantee card.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
I threw the box away so I don't know the model number! Would I have to look under the hob? I just want to know if I need to buy new pans!

You don't need to look under the hob right now because we have already confirmed your saucepans are incompatible with induction cooking. The 'U' code is simply the hob telling you it cannot detect a magnetic pan, which explains why they flash that code while your cast-iron casserole works perfectly. To be absolutely sure there isn't another issue, please try placing a large, flat-based pan that you know has a magnetic base on the zone and see if it heats up without flashing. If it does heat up normally, then you most likely just need to buy new induction-compatible pans for your saucepans.
